items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: I always figured, because I know he admired Hodges -- he didn't like him but he admired him.

ctx.x: And he sat there and he played, I believe, that solo that you didn't hear. On the train, we were sitting there and he played, and it was fantastic. I realize what the tune was, which of course, you know what the tune was, the basic chord changes. And then when a record came out I saw "Cottontail," Ben Webster, I think it was one of the first things he did as a special. And I said, that ain't the one that Ben played for me.

That's right, yeah. I guess he named that after Johnny Hodges then, because they called Hodges "Rabbit," and I always figured, because I know he admired Hodges -- he didn't like him but he admired him.
